arxiv-2301-13077.title: A sluggish random walk with subdiffusive spread
arxiv-2301-13077.creator: Aniket Zodage 1,2 , Rosalind J. Allen 3,4 , Martin R. Evans 4,5 , Satya N. Majumdar 5
arxiv-2301-13077.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Aniket Zodage 1,2 , Rosalind J. Allen 3,4 , Martin R. Evans 4,5 , Satya N. Majumdar 5. We study a one-dimensional sluggish random walk with space-dependent transition probabilities between nearest-neighbour lattice sites. Motivated by trap models of slow dynamics, we consider a model in which the trap depth increases logarithmically with distance from the origin.

arxiv-2302-05895.title: Discourse Structure Extraction from Pre-Trained and Fine-Tuned Language Models in Dialogues
arxiv-2302-05895.creator: Chuyuan Li 1, Patrick Huber 2, Wen Xiao 2
arxiv-2302-05895.description: Abstract Discourse processing suffers from data sparsity, especially for dialogues. As a result, we explore approaches to build discourse structures for dialogues, based on attention matrices from Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs). We investigate multiple tasks for fine-tuning and show that the dialogue-tailored Sentence Ordering task performs best.

arxiv-2302-11663.title: Public Key Encryption with Secure Key Leasing
arxiv-2302-11663.creator: Shweta Agrawal, Fuyuki Kitagawa, Ryo Nishimaki, Shota Yamada, Takashi Yamakawa
arxiv-2302-11663.description: Abstract We introduce the notion of public key encryption with secure key leasing (PKE-SKL). Our notion supports the leasing of decryption keys so that a leased key achieves the decryption functionality but comes with the guarantee that if the quantum decryption key returned by a user passes a validity test, then the user has lost the ability to decrypt.

arxiv-2501-13264.title: RAG-Reward: Optimizing RAG with Reward Modeling and RLHF
arxiv-2501-13264.creator: Hanning Zhang, Juntong Song, Juno Zhu, Yuanhao Wu, Tong Zhang, Cheng Niu
arxiv-2501-13264.description: Abstract Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) with relevant and up-to-date knowledge, improving their ability to answer knowledge-intensive questions. It has been shown to enhance both generation quality and trustworthiness. While numerous works have focused on improving retrieval, generation, and evaluation, the role of reward models in reinforcement learning for optimizing RAG remains underexplored.

arxiv-2510-17792.title: SoftMimic : Learning Compliant Whole-body Control from Examples
arxiv-2510-17792.creator: Gabriel B. Margolis, Michelle WangNolan Fey, Pulkit Agrawal
arxiv-2510-17792.description: Abstract We introduce SoftMimic , a framework for learning compliant whole-body control policies for humanoid robots from example motions. Imitating human motions with reinforcement learning allows humanoids to quickly learn new skills, but existing methods incentivize stiff control that aggressively corrects deviations from a reference motion, leading to brittle and unsafe behavior when the robot encounters unexpected contacts.

pmc-11459106.title: Toward Physiological Detection of a “Just-Right” Challenge Level for Motor Learning in Immersive Virtual Reality: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11459106.creator: Samory Houzangbe, Martin Lemay, Danielle E Levac
pmc-11459106.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMotor learning, a primary goal of pediatric rehabilitation, is facilitated when tasks are presented at a “just-right” challenge level—at the edge of the child’s current abilities, yet attainable enough to motivate the child in persistent efforts for success. Immersive virtual reality (VR) may be ideally suited for “just-right” task challenges because it enables precise adjustments of task parameters in motivating environments. Rehabilitation-specific VR tasks often use dynamic difficulty algorithms based on task performance to personalize task difficulty.

pmc-12629799.title: Sintilimab plus chemotherapy for first-line treatment of advanced pulmonary lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma: Phase 2 trial
pmc-12629799.creator: Xinqing Lin, Haiyi Deng, Nianxin Fang, Likun Chen, Rui Chen, Xiaohong Xie, Zhanhong Xie, Jiexia Zhang, Ming Liu, Laiyu Liu, Ni Sun, Fei Wang, Yilin Yang, Xinze Lv, Zhou Zhang, Shangli Cai, Ting Hou, Shiyue Li, Jianxing He, Chengzhi Zhou
pmc-12629799.description: SummaryPulmonary lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma (PLELC) is a unique non-small cell lung cancer associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), lacking a standard treatment. This phase 2 study evaluates sintilimab plus gemcitabine and carboplatin (4 cycles), followed by sintilimab maintenance in 30 untreated patients with locally advanced or metastatic PLELC. At a median follow-up of 42.4 months, the objective response rate is 73.

uslaw-usc-t22-s4357.title: 22 U.S.C. § 4357 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t22-s4357.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s4357.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 53B (Foreign Relations Of The United States Historical Series). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For purposes of this chapter— (1) the term “Advisory Committee” means the Advisory Committee on Historical Diplomatic Documentation for the Department of State; (2) the term “Historian” means the Historian of the Department of State or any successor.

uslaw-usc-t47-s1454.title: 47 U.S.C. § 1454 — Guard bands and unlicensed use
uslaw-usc-t47-s1454.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t47-s1454.description: United States Code, Title 47 (Telecommunications); Chapter 13 (Public Safety Communications And Electromagnetic Spectrum Auctions); Subchapter IV (Spectrum Auction Authority). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general Nothing in subparagraph (G) of section 309(j)(8) of this title or in section 1452 of this title shall be construed to prevent the Commission from using relinquished or other spectrum to implement band plans.
